newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ex-president must testify again on murders.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ex-president must testify again on murders.

text.p: Mexico's Attorney General said on Monday that former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari would have to testify again to prosecutors probing two 1994 political murders.

"With no doubt, that statement from Carlos Salinas de Gortari will have to be taken ... it will be taken. I cannot give you an exact date yet," Jorge Madrazo Cuellar, who took over as Attorney General earlier this month, told reporters.

Salinas, who lives in self-imposed exile in Ireland and denies having anything to do with the murders, has already testified in the March 23, 1994 murder of Luis Donaldo Colosio, the man who had been widely expected to succeed him as president.
He must now give evidence on the Sept. 28, 1994 murder of ruling party politician Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, for which Salinas' elder brother Raul Salinas is in jail on murder charges.
Madrazo said investigators, who flew to Dublin on Nov. 27 to take the ex-president's testimony on Colosio, would do so again in the Ruiz case as soon as a new special prosecutor was appointed.

Madrazo also said that the verdict on a set of human bones found buried in a ranch used by Raul Salinas was not yet complete. Madrazo's predecessor Antonio Lozano had alleged that the bones were the those of a missing ruling party legislator also wanted in the Ruiz case.

The wife of Raul Salinas alleged in a newspaper interview published on Monday, that prosecutors had faked evidence, bribed witnesses and distorted facts in their attempt to prove that her husband ordered the murder of Ruiz.

Paulina Castanon told the newspaper Reforma from Switzerland, where she is testifying in an investigation, that "there are fabricated documents and witnesses who follow instructions, (who are) threatened and rewarded," adding that lawyers had evidence to back her claims. "But I know that all this will be cleared up and the truth will come out."
